Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:10:1.english: Partially overlapping - Part of one [coin is] on its fellow, and part [is] on the ground.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:10:2.english: [He is] obligated to proclaim [his find] - Thus, [a case] like this is not the manner of falling.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:11:1.hebrew: של שלשה מלכים - קס"ד שלא היו צורותיהם שוות, שכל מלך כותב שמו וצורתו על מטבע שלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:11:1.english: Of three kings - [The Gemara] initially assumed that their images were not alike, for every king inscribes his name and his image on his coin.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:11:2.english: If [they] are arranged like towers - [Meaning] that they are not equal in their width and are placed as I explained.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:11:3.english: Even [coins] of one king - Where the image of all three of them is the same.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:1.hebrew: של מלך אחד כעין שלשה מלכים - כלומר, אפי' הן של מלך אחד, שצורת שלשתן שוה, והן כעין שלשה מלכים שחלוקין ברחבן ודומין לג' מטבעות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:1.english: Of one king, similar to three kings - That is to say, even if they are of one king, such that the image of all three of them is the same, yet they are similar to [coins of] three kings in that they differ in their width and resemble three [different] coins.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: והיכי דמי כגון שעשויין כמגדלין להכריז:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:2.english: This is the reading: "And what are the circumstances — such as where they are arranged in towers — [that one is obligated] to proclaim?"

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:3.english: Since all of them are like one another - [They are] equal in their width.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:4.hebrew: אע"ג דכי הדדי מנחי - זה על זה ולאו משלחפי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:4.english: Even though they are lying evenly together - [Directly] one upon the other and not staggered.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:5.hebrew: אימור [אתרמויי] אתרמי - דהכי נפל ואין זה הינוח, וסימן אין לו בהם, ואפי' מקום, דלא ידע היכן נפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:12:5.english: Say it happened by chance - That it fell this way, and this is not a deliberate placement, and he has no distinguishing mark on them — not even [their] location, since he does not know where it fell.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:1.hebrew: אפי' של מלך אחד מכריז - הואיל ומטבעות הוו זו ע"ג זו, יש כאן סימן, דלא אתרמי דנפול הכי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:1.english: Even [coins] of one king, he proclaims - Since [the] coins were one on top of another, there is a distinguishing mark here, for it does not happen by chance that they fall like this.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:2.hebrew: ופרכינן מאי מכריז מנין - כך וכך מטבעות מצאתי, וזה בא ונתן סימן: זו ע"ג זו מצאתם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:2.english: And we ask: What does he proclaim? Number - [The finder proclaims,] "I found such-and-such [a number of] coins," and this [owner] comes and gives a distinguishing mark: "You found them one on top of another."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:3.hebrew: טבעא מכריז - "מטבעות מצאתי", הלכך תרי לאו סימנא הוא, דמיעוט מטבעות ב':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:13:3.english: [He] proclaims coins - [He proclaims,] "I found coins"; therefore, two is not a distinguishing mark, for the minimum [number of] coins is two.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:1.english: Like a bracelet - [They are] lying in a circle, like an armlet.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:2.english: Like a line - One next to the other.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:3.hebrew: כחצובה - כג' רגלי קנקן, כל אחד כנגד אויר של שני, כזה * _ *:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:3.english: Like a tripod - Like three legs of a pitcher, each one opposite the space between [the other] two, like this: * _ *.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:4.hebrew: כסולם - רוב אמצעי על התחתון, ורוב העליון על האמצעי, כמו מעלות שקורין אשקולינו"ש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:14:4.english: Like a ladder - Most of the middle [coin is] upon the bottom [one], and most of the top [one is] upon the middle [one], like steps that are called *eschalons* [in Old French].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:15:1.english: Resolve from this - [From that statement] of Rav Nachman, [resolve] one [of the dilemmas].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:15:2.hebrew: כל שאילו מכניס כו' - וכי הוו כסולם, ניטלים בבת אחת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:15:2.english: Any [case] where if one inserts, etc. - And when they are like a ladder, they are lifted all at once.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:1:1.hebrew: שלשה מטבעות זו ע"ג זו - בגמרא מפרש סימנייהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:1:1.english: Three coins, one atop another - In the Gemara, [it] explains their identifying marks.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:2:1.english: The reason [is] that he found, etc. - It is [only] there that [we] say that the produce belongs to the owner of the vessel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:2:2.hebrew: הא כלי ולפניו פירות - הרי אלו הפירות של מוצאן. ואע"פ שהכלי לבעל הסימן, את הכלי יחזיר ואת הפירות יעכב לו, ולא אמרינן מהאי מנא נפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:2:2.english: But [if he found] a vessel and produce before it - This produce belongs to the one who found it. And even though the vessel belongs to the owner of the identifying mark, he returns the vessel and keeps the produce for himself, and we do not say [that] it fell from this vessel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:2:3.hebrew: מקצתן בכלי כו' - הדבר מוכיח דהנך דעל גבי קרקע דהנך הוא, וחייב להחזירם למי שיתן סימן בכלי, וכן מעות לבעל הכיס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:2:3.english: Some of them in the vessel, etc. - The matter proves that those on the ground are [part] of those [in the vessel], and he is obligated to return them to whoever provides an identifying mark for the vessel; and similarly, [the] coins to the owner of the pouch.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג - מצא דבר שאין בו סימן בצד דבר שיש בו סימן, כגון מעות לפני כיס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:1.english: This is the reading - "He found an item on which there is no distinguishing mark alongside an item on which there is a distinguishing mark," for example, coins in front of a pouch.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:2.hebrew: חייב להכריז - על הכל, וינתנו המעות לבעל הכיס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:2.english: He is obligated to proclaim - Regarding everything, and the money shall be given to the owner of the purse.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:3.hebrew: בא בעל סימן ונטל את שלו - את הכיס, ואמר "אין המעות שלי", זכה הלה במעות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:3:3.english: The owner of [an item with] a distinguishing mark came and took his - [i.e.,] the purse, and said, "The money is not mine," [then] the other [person] acquires the money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:4:2.hebrew: בכובא וכיתנא - גיגית מוטלת ופשתן לפניה, דודאי האי פשתן לאו מכובא נפל, דאי מינה נפל הוה משתייר בה. והוא הדין לכיס ולפניו מעות, מהאי טעמא. והא דקתני חייב, בצנא ופירי, דעבידי דשרקי ונפלי מיניה כולהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:4:2.english: With a tub and flax - [This refers to] a tub lying [on its side] with flax in front of it, for certainly this flax did not fall from the tub, since if it had fallen from it, [some] would have remained in it. And the same law applies to a purse with coins in front of it, for this [same] reason. And that which [the baraita] teaches [that he is] obligated [to proclaim refers] to a basket and produce, for they tend to slide out and all of them fall from it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:5:1.english: This [baraita] that teaches [he is] obligated [is] where [some] remained - And it can be said [that] those [fruits] that are outside fell from it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:6:1.hebrew: והא דלא אשתייר - כיון דסתם צנא יש לו אוגנין כפולים לתוכו, אי מתוכו נפל, הוה משתייר ביה, דאוגנין מעכבי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:6:1.english: And that [case] where nothing remained - Since an ordinary basket has rims folded inward, if [the produce] had fallen from inside it, [some] would have remained in it, because the rims hold it back.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:7:1.hebrew: הא דאית ליה אוגנין - לאו מיניה נפל, דאי מיניה נפל, הוה משתייר ביה מידי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:7:1.english: This [refers to a case] where [the basket] has a rim - It did not fall from it, for if it had fallen from it, something would have remained in it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:1.hebrew: ש"מ מנין הוי סימן - דאי לאו הכי, מאי סימן איכא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:1.english: Conclude from it [that] number is a distinguishing mark - For if not so, what distinguishing mark is there?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:2.hebrew: תני צבור פירות - דאין כאן מנין, מאי סימניה? מקום. דכיון דצבורין, הינוח הוה, ויהיב סימנא: במקום פלוני הנחתים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:2.english: Teach: "A pile of produce" - For there is no number here; what is its distinguishing mark? Location. For since they are piled up, it is [a case of] deliberate placement, and he gives the distinguishing mark: "In such-and-such a place I placed them."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:3.hebrew: תני צבורי פירות - סימני מנין דהוי, מדחי ליה. לא הא תפשוט ולא הא תפשוט:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:8:3.english: Teach: "Piles of produce" - [Since] it is a distinguishing mark of number, it pushes it [i.e., the proof for location] off. You can resolve neither this [question] nor that [question].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:9:1.hebrew: והוא שעשוין כמגדלין - לקמיה מפרש ששלשתן רחבין זה מזה, ומניח מלמטה את הרחב, ועליו את הבינוני, ועליון הוא הקצר שבכולן, כמגדל זה העשוי היסוד רחב ומקצר ועולה. וכי מנחי הכי, לאו דרך נפילה הוה אלא דרך הינוח, והיה דעתו לחזור ולטלן ושכח. הלכך, נוטל ומכריז, וזה בא ונותן סימן ואומר: מגדלין היו עשויין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:9:1.english: And [only] when they are arranged like towers - Further on [the Gemara] explains that the three of them are [progressively] wider than one another, and one places the wide one at the bottom, and upon it the medium-sized one, and the top one is the narrowest of all of them, like a tower that is made [with] a wide base and narrows as it rises. And when they lie like this, it is not by way of falling, rather by way of [deliberate] placement, and it was his intention to return and take them, and he forgot. Therefore, [the finder] takes [them] and proclaims [the find], and this [owner] comes and gives an identifying mark, and says: "They were arranged as towers."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:9:2.hebrew: ג' מטבעות - שאין דומות זו לזו ברחבן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25a:9:2.english: Three coins - That are not similar to one another in their width.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:10:1.hebrew: הא גופא קשיא - אמתני' לא פריך, דמצינן למימר דג' מטבעות היינו פירוש דצבורי מעות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:10:1.english: "This itself is difficult" - [The Gemara] does not raise a difficulty against the Mishnah, because we can say that "three coins" [in the baraita] is the explanation of "piles of coins" [in the Mishnah].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:4:1.hebrew: הא בכובא וכיתנא - פי' רש"י דמתני' בכובא וכיתנא, וקשה דקתני: "מצא פירות". וי"א דכיתנא אקרי פירי, כדאמרינן (בבראשית רבה): "ויבא קין מפרי האדמה" — זרע פשתן הביא; ודוחק. ונראה דמתני' בצנא ופירי, דכיון דאין הפירות מחוברים יחד, אילו מן הכלי נפלו — היה קצת נשאר מהם בכלי; אבל פשתן שקשור ביחד, יכול להיות שבכלי היה ונפל. ור"ח פי' דפריך אמאי דקאמר "מקצתן על גבי קרקע — חייב להכריז", ורמינהו: "מצא דבר כו' בא בעל סימן ונטל את שלו — זכה המוצא במה שבידו"; היינו מה שבחוץ, אע"פ שיש בפנים קצת פירות, ואפילו בעל כלי אומר שכולן שלו. ולפי זה גרס בסמוך: "הא והא דאשתיירי ביה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:4:1.english: This [refers] to a container and flax - Rashi explained that the Mishnah [refers] to a container and flax, and it is difficult, for [the Mishnah] teaches: "If one found produce." And some say that flax is called produce, as we say (in Bereishit Rabbah): "And Cain brought of the fruit of the ground" — he brought flaxseed; but [this] is forced. And it appears that the Mishnah [refers] to a basket and produce, for since the produce is not connected together, had it fallen from the vessel, some of it would have remained in the vessel; however, flax, which is tied together, could have been in the vessel and fallen [out]. And Rabbeinu Chananel explained that [the Gemara] asks on that which it said, "part of them on the ground — he is obligated to proclaim [them]," and raises a contradiction: "If one found something, etc., the owner of the identifying mark came and took his own — the finder acquires what is in his hand"; that is, what is outside [the vessel], even though there is some produce inside, and even if the owner of the vessel says that all of it is his. And according to this, he reads shortly [below]: "Both this and that [refer to a case] where some remained in it."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:8:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה מנין הוי סימן - אע"ג דפשיטא ליה לעיל מדמשקל הוי סימן, מדה ומנין נמי הוי סימן — בעי לאוכוחי הכא ממתני'. ולעיל (בבא מציעא דף כד) נמי, דקתני "אבל מצא שנים חייב", לא קאמר ש"מ מנין הוי סימן (דלא אלימא ליה ברייתא למפשט מינה); אי נמי, דמצי למדחי דמנין וחרוזא הוי סימן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:8:1.english: Conclude from it [that] number is a distinguishing mark - Even though it was obvious to [the Gemara] earlier [that] since weight is a distinguishing mark, measure and number are also distinguishing marks, [nonetheless] it seeks to prove [it] here from the Mishnah. And earlier (Bava Metzia 24) as well, where [the Baraita] teaches: "But if he found two, he is obligated [to proclaim]," it does not say "Conclude from it [that] number is a distinguishing mark" ([because] the Baraita is not strong enough for [the Gemara] to resolve [the question] from it); or alternatively, because it could reject [the proof by saying] that number together with a stringing [of the items] is a distinguishing mark.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:9:1.hebrew: והוא שעשויין כמגדלין - אי מנין הוי סימן, במה שעשויין כמגדלין ידעינן דדרך הינוח הוה, ובתרי לא סגי, דטבעא מכריז; אבל אם מקום הוי סימן, אפילו בתרי ועשויין כמגדלין ידעינן דדרך הינוח הוה. דאי בתרי אפי' עשויין כמגדלין לא ידעינן דדרך הינוח הוה, דאימור דרך נפילה הוה דאתרמי הכי, א"כ לקמן מאי פריך (אר' יוחנן): "מאי אריא תלתא, אפי' בתרי סגי"? וי"ל דשפיר משני: "טבעא מכריז":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25a:9:1.english: And [this applies only] where they are arranged like towers - If number is a distinguishing mark, [then] through the fact that they are arranged like towers we know that it was [placed] in a deliberate manner, and two [coins] do not suffice because [the finder] proclaims "coins" [in the plural]; but if location is a distinguishing mark, [then] even with two [coins] that are arranged like towers we know that it was [placed] in a deliberate manner. For if [you argue that] with two [coins], even when arranged like towers, we do not know that it was [placed] in a deliberate manner — because one could say it was by way of falling that it happened so — [then] if so, later, what does [the Gemara] ask (on Rabbi Yoḥanan): "Why specifically three? Even two suffice!"? And one can answer that [Ravina] answers well: "He proclaims 'coins.'"
